_note: The second heart events (data/events/heart_<villager>_5.json): one scene per villager when their heart band first reaches 5 and the farmer talks to them, after the band 3 one. One part per villager, started at its id. Our own scenes.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There you are. I was just writing to my son in the city. He writes back twice a year, if the rice is good.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I told him the old farm has someone in it again. That the lamp is lit in the evenings and the field is turned.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I hope you don't mind. An old woman likes to have news to send.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: ...The children here call me Grandma. You could too, if it wouldn't feel strange.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. Then I'll put that in the letter too. Mind you eat properly, grandchild.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ha! Straight as a bamboo pole. I like that better, truth be told.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I saw it! The black carp, this morning, right under the willow. It looked at me!

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I had my net and everything. And then I just... didn't. It looked too old to bother.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Don't tell anyone I went soft. I'll catch something worse to make up for it.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I had my net and I didn't use it. You promised, so I thought I should keep it too. Partners, right?

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Hey... when I'm big, could I farm too? Mom says the field is hard work. Is it?

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Hard, and worth it. Come help at harvest and see.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Really? I'm bringing my own basket. A big one!

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Look what came in the mail. Paint! Real lacquer red, for the sign over the door.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Father's lettering has nearly worn away. I used to think repainting it would be like rubbing him out.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: But a store that looks tired makes people walk past. And I'm not minding it anymore. It's mine now.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Which should go on the new sign, do you think?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: The old name. Yes. He'd grumble about my brushwork either way.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Mine? ...I was hoping somebody would say that, so I didn't have to.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Thank you. You're the first person I asked. Somehow it had to be you.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Hold out your hand. No, the other one.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: A door bell. Iron, folded nine times, cooled in snow water. It rings a little lower than you'd think.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: My teacher hung one on this smithy the day I opened it. Said a house with a bell is a house people come back to.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: I've only made three. One for my teacher's grave, one for this door. And now that one.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I'll hang it where I hear it every morning.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Good. ...Don't make a fuss. Go on, the field won't hoe itself.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: You came. Sit for one cup? There's something I want to ask somebody, and it can't be anybody.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: A tea merchant from the city wants to buy the teahouse. A proper shop, he says, with a sign you could read from the mine.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Everyone in the village says 'whatever you think best, Fumi.' Which is no help at all. What do you think?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: You told me the truth about the bean paste. It tastes like hers now, by the way. So tell me true again.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Keep it. The road wouldn't be the same without your kettle on.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: ...I told him no before he'd finished his tea. I only wanted to hear someone say it out loud.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Now drink up, before it goes cold. I'm not pouring you a third. Well. Maybe a third.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: The kiln's cracked. My father built it the year I was born. It's done.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I'll build a new one this winter. Creek clay, packed by hand, sealed while it's wet. Takes two days without stopping.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Takes two pairs of hands, really. I've never asked anybody for anything. So. I'm asking.

choices.text: I'd only get in the way.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Good. The old man would laugh. He always said I'd never ask.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hm. Honest. Then come and see the first smoke. That's the best part anyway.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Fumi says I don't talk enough. Tell her I talked to you. That'll keep her quiet a while.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Wait there. My eyes aren't what they were, and I want a pair of young hands.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: My wife sewed new bibs for the jizo by the lane every autumn. Red ones. I've patched the old ones since, but this autumn the needle won't stay in my fingers.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The cloth is on the shelf by my door. Would you tie them on? Only the bibs. I'll watch.

choices.text: Show me how she did it first.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Knot at the back, loose enough for a child's finger. ...Good. She'd say it's crooked, and retie it herself.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Over, under, and a bow like a rabbit's ear. ...Yes. Like that. You have the hands for it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Red again. Now the lane looks lived in. Come up for tea some day. I make it badly.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Can I tell you my New Year's wish? It's late enough now that it won't spoil.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A craft shop in the city saw my sandals at the fair. They want me there, weaving for them all year. Good pay. A room with a window.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I wished to know what to do. Then I climbed the hill every afternoon, and the hill said nothing. So I'm asking you.

choices.text: Go if it calls you. Come back often.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: ...Would it? Genzo would never say so. But he'd sit by the well alone, and the racks would stand empty in fall.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You'd let me go, just like that? ...That makes it easier to stay, oddly. Nobody's holding the door.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I'll stay. Sayo can sell my sandals at her store, and the city can walk down here to buy them. Thank you for listening.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Can I show you something? This tin was my wife's. Pumpkin seed, saved from her mother's vines, and hers before that.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Pumpkins were her crop. After she was gone I couldn't put them in. Eight years the tin has sat on the shelf. Nana doesn't even remember the vines.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Seed this old may not come up at all. But it won't come up in a tin, either. I've been working up to it. So, grower to grower...

choices.text: Grow some on my farm too.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: By the fence, where she'd look for them. ...Yes. If they come up, they should come up there.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Half here, half with you. If one patch fails, the other won't. That's a real grower's answer. She'd have said the same.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Here, your share, in a fresh packet. Sow it thick. And when Nana cries over the first vine, pretend you didn't see.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: They want to pull out the ferry landing. The bridge upstream does the job, the village head says. Nobody's crossed with me since spring.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Father's pole is still up in the rafters. I keep oiling it. Silly, isn't it?

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: So tell me straight. Do I keep the ferry, or let the river have it?

choices.text: Keep it for the slow way.
Let it go. You'd still be you.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The slow way... I like that. I'll hang a bell on the landing. Anyone who rings it gets taken across, even at night.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: ...Huh. Nobody's ever told me that. That I'd still be me without it.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Either way, the traps stay. The river and I aren't done arguing yet. Thanks for listening, farmer.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome says I'll lead the New Year rite alone this year. Alone. In front of the whole village.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather never wrote the words down. I've got Tome's version in a notebook, but what if my mind goes white?

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: What do I do? Tell me something, anything.

choices.text: Write the words on my sleeve.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Inside the sleeve, where nobody sees... You're terrible. I love it. Tome must never know.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Now? To you? ...All right. Don't look at me. Look at the fox.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Thank you. Whatever happens at midnight, I'll remember someone stood on this step with me.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I opened Mother's stencil box last night. Two hundred patterns. Waves, cranes, hemp leaves. All hers.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The school in the city taught me to make my own. But who wants a new pattern from someone who left?

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: So tell me. Do I dye her patterns, or cut my own?

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Her patterns, my hands. ...Then she's still dyeing with me. I hadn't thought of it like that.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: My own. ...You say it like it's simple. Maybe it is. I'll start with the wildflowers by the lane.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Thank you. I've asked the vats about this for a month. They never answer.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Head office wrote. To me, for once. They want a van to bring the valley's post twice a week, and the rounds on foot to stop.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Twice a week. Tome would wait three days for her son's letter. The doctor's medicine would sit in a sorting room.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: They said I could drive the van. Or I could tell them no. What would you do?

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: On foot. Every door, every day. ...Yes. I'll write them the longest letter of my life.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Drive it myself. Then the van would at least know whose gate sticks and whose dog bites. Huh. That might work.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Thanks. I talk all day and never ask anyone anything. That was nice, for once.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Can I show you something? Don't tell Kota. It's a map of the sky. I drew it on the back of a seed sack.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Granny Kiku says Mama is up with the stars. I don't remember her. So I picked one for her: the small one that blinks. She sounds like somebody who blinks a lot.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Dad hasn't got a star yet. He just looks at the ground. Which one should be his?

choices.text: The big one that never moves.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Big and steady and right where you left it. That's Dad all over! He'll say it's too bright. He'll like it.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Right beside Mama's? ...Yes. So they can blink at each other. I'm drawing it now.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Here, two cucumbers from my own row. For a friend who looks at maps. Don't tell Kota I like you.
